why: Both routes pin Boundary Camp at the identical coordinate 48.8875,-121.5236. USGS ground there is 4,406 ft; Poltergeist claims 4,410 and this route 3,800. NPS (nps.gov/noca/planyourvisit/copper-ridge-trail.htm) gives 'To Boundary Camp: 5 miles (8 km) 2,000 ft gain (610 m) / 620 ft loss (189 m)' from the 3,100 ft Hannegan trailhead, which corroborates ~4,400 and refutes 3,800.

This route's own recorded track (330 points) passes 0.01 mi from the sibling pass coordinate, at 3.82 mi along. The stored pin is also on the track but 0.54 mi earlier, on 4,472 ft ground against a 5,100 claim: on the climb to the pass, not at it. The sibling coordinate reads 5,072, the pass. Crooked Thumb pins the pass identically.

The stored pin is on this route's recorded track but 0.28 mi short of the sibling camp (which is 0.04 mi off the same track), on 4,573 ft ground: partway down from the pass. Poltergeist and Indian Mountain both pin the camp at 48.8875,-121.5236, ground 4,406.
2,600 ft is 1,800 ft below the camp: NPS puts it 2,000 ft up and 620 ft down from the 3,100 ft trailhead, and the ground at the camp reads 4,406. Copied with the coordinate from the same sibling pin.

The pin is 2.27 mi from Park Lakes (OSM 47.4490859,-121.2990156), and the route's own track passes the real lakes 0.11 mi off. But copying the real position would make the next stored leg impossible (to the gully turnoff, 1.0 mi stored for ~2.1 mi straight), and the list orders the basin BEFORE the turnoff below Chikamin Pass, which the PCT reaches first. Name, order and position disagree; no single op fixes it without guessing. Its 442 ft height gap is below the ground box's 500 ft bar.

The coordinate is Copper Creek Camp (0.2 mi from the creek's mapped mouth, on the route's sketch line), and the 7 mi distance and 3,400 ft height fit it, not Boundary Camp (NPS: 5 mi; Copper Creek 2.5 mi below). The note describes the first-night camp 'near the park boundary'. Read as naming the two usual first-night camps, the label is not wrong; renaming it would mean rewriting the note prose too. Nothing about it is impossible.

Claims 3,100 ft on 2,660 ft ground (gap 440) and Elwha Snow Finger claims 4,300 on 3,547 (gap 753). audit:waypoint-elevations --ground (2026-10-01) places neither beyond what the terrain can explain, and no sibling route pins the basin to copy from. The route has no gpx, so no track contradicts it either.
